decisions.title: resn's page-wide WebGL scene and its canvas-drawn menu labels
decisions.why: resn's whole header is four independently pinned controls with no <header>, its menu labels are per-item 2D canvases (no DOM text at 375 at all), and its background is a persistent three.js scene. Its own teardown records that no built Spec 38 effect matches and that the scene passes no Tier W test. Cloning canvas labels would DELETE real text, which the framework must not do.
options: (a) Trim resn from the 13-reference clone roster and build M-08 for the other four references that need it.
(b) Keep resn as the 13th clone: build M-08, render the labels as real DOM text, and approximate the scene with a Tier V or an existing fx field; record the divergence.
(c) Admit a new Tier W page-background scene for it under Spec 38 §1's five-part test.
decisions.recommendation: (b). It keeps the roster at 13 and keeps M-08 (needed by five references, not one) on its merits, without a tier admission that would have to be justified for one page. The canvas-label divergence is recorded the same way as the accessibility ones.

decisions.amended: 2026-09-24 (U-9, D1150): the lamalama close-on-scroll carve-out necessarily drops the page scroll lock while it is set (a locked page cannot scroll, so the route could never fire); it closes only on pointer-driven scrolling and never on touch input. decisions.title: Accessibility divergences: a faithful clone would be LESS accessible than its reference
decisions.why: 9 of 13 triggers omit aria-expanded, 2 are unfocusable <div>s, buck's button has no accessible name, wearecollins' aria-controls dangles; 7 references do not close on Escape; 6 let the page scroll behind an open drawer; 6 let Tab leave; 10 of 13 fail the 44px target. SGS emits the accessible pole of every one of these and cannot emit the other.
options: (a) Keep SGS's accessible default everywhere; record each divergence at clone time so Bean's eye does not read a correct clone as wrong.
(b) Add opt-outs so a clone can reproduce the reference exactly.
(c) Decide per clone.
decisions.recommendation: (a), with ONE carve-out: lamalama's close-on-scroll is a design choice, not an a11y defect, so it gets an attribute (in U-9). wearecollins' 'm' hotkey and resn's history-back closer are also not defects but are single-reference and can wait.

decisions.why: Seven references stay open and reflow, two deliberately close, and both drafts keep an open FLAG while the surface is not rendered. store.js listens for no resize at all, so SGS has one unstated behaviour where the references have three. A drawer left open while its trigger disappears is a trap.
options: (a) Close the drawer when the viewport crosses collapsePoint; stay open and reflow otherwise. One rule, no attribute.
(b) The same rule plus an attribute so the other two behaviours are reachable.
(c) Leave it unstated.
decisions.recommendation: (a). It is the safe behaviour, it matches away and fantasy, and the difference the other seven references would see is invisible unless someone resizes across the breakpoint with the drawer open.

decisions.title: For Bean's two drafts, clone the INTENT or the RENDER
decisions.why: halcyon and indus-foods declare sticky (an ancestor overflow-x:hidden stops it), a 340ms panel entry and a 420ms/55ms item stagger (a componentDidUpdate arity bug throws before either runs), and an Escape handler that only clears the desktop state. Source and render disagree on four separate things and both are recorded.
options: (a) Clone the INTENT; the render is a bug in the draft's own runtime, not a requirement.
(b) Clone the RENDER as measured.
(c) Per row.
decisions.recommendation: (a) — as all three source lists already assumed. Worth stating explicitly because it means the panel-entry shape in M-31 is a real requirement, not an artefact.

decisions.title: The two drafts' 768 rows are MOBILE, not tablet
decisions.why: halcyon collapses at 940 and indus-foods at 960, both breakpoint-verified to within 1px. Reading their 768 cells as a tablet tier would invent a tablet layout neither design has.
options: (a) Read them as mobile throughout Wave 3C and Wave 4.
(b) Re-capture both at a real tablet width (e.g. 1000px).
decisions.recommendation: (a), and add (b) to the DEC-04 re-capture run if it happens anyway — a 1000px row would give those two drafts a genuine tablet tier for the first time.

decisions.title: Lottie and live-canvas logo substrates
decisions.why: buck's mark is a Lottie JSON and lamalama's is a live 2D canvas. Neither is an image, svgAnimationSource accepts a media-library .svg only, and inline SVG paste is banned as an XSS risk. Neither has a Spec 38 tier.
options: (a) Out of Wave 3C: clone both as stills and record the divergence.
(b) Admit a Lottie player and a canvas-2D mark (a new runtime plus a new tier admission).
decisions.recommendation: (a). Two references, a decorative mark, and a new runtime is a poor trade against the eight missing furniture blocks in U-12.

decisions.title: Whole-bar-as-trigger (lamalama)
decisions.why: lamalama's entire header pill IS the menu button, and its opened pill IS the panel. SGS's trigger is always a discrete control inside the row. The panel half is already reachable (the --sgs-mm-panel-width override repositionPanel writes when the header measures as inset from both edges); the trigger half is not.
options: (a) Add a triggerMode value meaning 'the row's own surface is the trigger' (U-14).
(b) Clone lamalama with a discrete trigger and record the divergence.
decisions.recommendation: (a). The pill header is already built and matches lamalama's measured box, so the surface-trigger is the one missing piece of an otherwise complete reference — and lamalama's large-hit-area pattern is the accessible one, which makes it worth having generally.
decisions.resolution: Built in U-14 (2026-09-25) as a SEPARATE attribute, sgs/nav-bar-menu::triggerSurface (tier on/off), not a fourth triggerMode value (Bean, with both council members): triggerMode chooses what the button shows, the surface chooses its hit area, so a surface keeps every presentation (lamalama's bars, or a word). Live: the burger's ::after measured 1200 x 67.47 = the row.

decisions.title: The drawer's close chrome: keep FR-36-6's undeletable x, or make it optional
decisions.why: nav-drawer/render.php emits the drawer's own x unconditionally — '$close_html = sprintf("<button type=\"button\" class=\"sgs-nav-drawer__close\" data-sgs-nav-close...")' under the comment 'The x button itself remains fixed, undeletable chrome in EVERY style (FR-36-6)'. NINE of thirteen references replace the burger IN PLACE with the header still visible and NO close control inside the drawer. So every clone of those nine renders a second close control the reference never had, and the plan's own W3C-2 target ('the drawer omits a separate top close row where they omit it') cannot be met. FR-36-6 was an accessibility choice, which makes this the same shape of call as DEC-02 — but unlike DEC-02 the accessible outcome survives either way, because the in-place burger IS a real button carrying aria-expanded.
options: (a) Keep FR-36-6 as an absolute: the drawer always carries its own x, and the nine in-place references are cloned with an extra control, recorded as a deliberate divergence.

(b) Amend FR-36-6: the drawer's own x becomes optional per closeStyle and per tier, required only when no other visible, keyboard-reachable close control is live — which is exactly the non-modal + burger-morph case the nine references use.
(c) Per clone.
decisions.recommendation: (b). The owner's stated W3C-2 intent IS the in-place swap, and the accessibility floor is not lowered by it: with modality='non-modal' the header burger stays live, keyboard-reachable and aria-expanded, so a close control is always reachable. It needs the amendment written into Spec 36 (with the 'only when another live close control exists' condition) before U-11 builds the gate.

decisions.title: The Wave 3C scope floor: six families are needed by two references or fewer
decisions.why: M-10 (magnet strength, 2), M-20 (away's callout row, 1), M-24 (sibling dim, 2), M-25 (two-copy label roll, 2), M-47 (multi-open accordion, 1) and M-08 (detaching trigger, 2 after re-scoping). Together they are a real slice of U-6, U-8, U-9, U-11 and U-14. The list has never asked whether a family needed by one or two references is in scope this wave, and the answer changes the size of four units.
options: (a) Build them all: every reference must be clonable, so a 1-reference gap is still a gap (the plan's own TEST says a row with no covering attribute is a gap unit, never a trimmed reference).
(b) Set a floor at 3 references for Wave 3C and park the rest with the reference they block named, revisiting at Wave 4 if a clone actually stalls.
(c) Floor at 3, except where the fix is small (M-10 is two attributes whose read side already exists; M-47 is two lines).
decisions.recommendation: (c). It keeps the plan's no-trimmed-reference rule honest for the cheap ones and stops a 1-reference structural change (M-08's detaching chip) sizing U-14 as if it were a wave-defining unit. It needs the owner to say which side of the line M-24 and M-25 fall on, since both need new markup rather than a new value.

decisions.title: Which of U-12's eight furniture blocks to build now
decisions.why: U-12 is the only high-size unit that is unconditionally parallel-safe, and it is the widest single gap (8 references). But it is eight new blocks — a live local-time clock, a language switch, a country/store selector, a back-to-top button, a wishlist, an account/log-in link, a theme toggle and a site-wide sound mute — which is eight builds, not one unit to sign whole. Four of them are ordinary commercial furniture the framework will need for client work regardless of this wave.
options: (a) All eight this wave.

(b) The four that block the most references and are reusable beyond nav: local-time clock (buck, studionamma), language switch (dogstudio, studionamma, lamalama), back-to-top (lusion) and account/log-in (away, butcherbox); park the store selector, wishlist, theme toggle and sound mute.
(c) None this wave: record them as clone-time divergences and build them when a client build asks.
decisions.recommendation: (b). It is the only option that keeps U-12 parallel-safe AND finishable, and every one of the four is furniture a paying client site needs anyway, so the work is not spent on the reference roster alone. The owner picks the four, not the engineer, because the trade is business value against clone completeness.

engineering_notes.title: The z-index attribute's default value
engineering_notes.text: The attribute is not in question (a hardcoded wrapper default that overrides transferred CSS is a cheat to remove). The remaining choice — default 100 vs unset — is a code default with a canary regression test, so it is an engineering call inside U-1. Build it as a per-tier attribute defaulting to 100: that cannot regress an existing composed header while making all eleven measured values (9 to 10000, plus auto) reachable, and wearecollins needs the per-tier half (999 at 375, 9 above).

engineering_notes.title: Multi-open accordions in the drawer
engineering_notes.text: A named `<details>` group is exclusive by construction and away@768 measured two panels open at once (669.5px and 1229.9px). Adding an `accordionExclusive` boolean that drops the `name` attribute when false is a two-line change in the markup builder; the only owner-shaped question is the DEFAULT, and single-open is right for three of the four accordion references, so default true. Engineering, inside U-9.
